items.item: Lymphedema compression garments, wraps and bandaging supplies
items.indication: Diagnosed lymphedema with a clinician order
items.policy_summary: A dedicated benefit began January 1, 2024. Eligible prescribed garments, wraps and supplies are covered. Part B deductible and 20% coinsurance generally apply.
items.comparison: Historical coverage gap versus current benefit; lymphedema versus no lymphedema
items.disparity_evidence: A 2015 cost-diary study found higher patient costs among breast-cancer survivors with lymphedema. It predates the new benefit.
items.evidence_type: National coverage change; observational patient-cost evidence
items.limitations: No male/female matched comparison. Coverage does not remove all out-of-pocket costs.
items.next_question: Have costs, use and claim denials changed since the 2024 benefit?

items.policy_summary: NCD 280.6 allows home pumps after a four-week conservative trial with no significant improvement or significant remaining symptoms. Advanced devices have additional requirements.
items.comparison: Standard versus advanced devices; coverage versus practical access
items.disparity_evidence: A 2022 review found varied insurer policies. Those insurer-level results do not establish Medicare denial rates.
items.evidence_type: National conditional coverage; broader insurer policy analysis
items.limitations: Policy presence is not claim approval, access or a sex-based payment comparison.
items.next_question: Compare denial reasons, device requirements and patient costs across indications and sexes.

studies.citation: Dean LT et al. Drivers of cost differences between US breast cancer survivors with or without lymphedema. J Cancer Surviv. 2019;13:804–814.
studies.design: Mixed methods: monthly cost diaries and interviews
studies.finding: Mean monthly direct costs were $355 with lymphedema versus $160 without. Higher costs extended beyond lymphedema treatment alone.
studies.limitation: Self-reported costs; socioeconomic ability to pay; no matched male comparator; predates 2024 Medicare benefit.
studies.relevance: Historical financial burden relevant to cancer survivorship; does not establish current noncoverage.

studies.citation: Lynn JV et al. Cross-Sectional Analysis of Insurance Coverage for Lymphedema Treatments in the United States. JAMA Surg. 2023;158:920–926.
studies.population: 67 insurers representing 88.7% of the US market
studies.payer: Major US insurers; not a Medicare-specific audit
studies.finding: Coverage with authorization: nonprogrammable pumps 55/67 insurers, programmable pumps 53/67, debulking 13/67 and physiologic surgery 5/67.
studies.limitation: Published policies, not actual claims; no sex-controlled comparison; predates the 2024 Medicare compression-item benefit.
studies.relevance: Identifies broader lymphedema coverage variation; Medicare-specific findings require separate verification.
